第 40 章 How Do Individual Contributors Get Stuck?独立贡献者怎么卡住的？

Camille Fournier / 卡米尔·福尼耶

— 第 121 页 —

As a new manager, you will become responsible for providing feedback to the people on your team. If you aren't a naturally critical person but you want to give someone a valuable insight, you might find this task daunting. To that end, I suggest the following: Pay attention to how they get stuck.

作为新经理，你将负责给团队成员提供反馈。如果你天生不是一个爱批评的人但你想给某人有价值的洞察，你可能觉得这个任务令人畏惧。为此，我建议：注意他们怎么卡住的。

Everyone has at least one area on which they tend to get stuck. An activity that serves as an attractive sidetrack. A task they will do anything to avoid. With a bit of observation, you can begin to see the places where your team members get stuck. This is a super power for many reasons, but at a baseline, it is great for when you need to write a review and want to provide useful constructive feedback.

每个人至少有一个容易卡住的领域。一个有吸引力的旁支活动。一个他们做什么都想避免的任务。稍微观察一下，你就能开始看到团队成员在哪里卡住。这是一个超能力，原因很多，但基线来说，它在你需要写评估、想提供有用的建设性反馈时非常好。

How do people get sidetracked? How do people get stuck? The lists that follow (which are not comprehensive) can get you started.

人们怎么跑偏？人们怎么卡住？以下列表（不全面）可以帮你开始。

Individual contributors often get sidetracked by:

独立贡献者经常被以下事情带偏：

  • Brainstorming/architecture: "I must have thought through all edge cases of all parts of everything before I can begin this project."头脑风暴/架构：「我必须把一切所有部分的所有边界情况都想清楚才能开始这个项目。」
  • Researching possible solutions forever (often accompanied by desire to do a "bakeoff" where they build prototypes in different platforms/languages/etc.).永远在研究可能的方案（通常伴随着想做「烘焙大赛」——在不同平台/语言里建原型）。
  • Refactoring: "This code could be cleaner and everything would be just so much easier if we cleaned this up… and this up… and…"重构：「这段代码可以更干净，如果我们清理一下这个……和这个……那就会容易太多……」
  • Helping other people instead of doing their assigned tasks.帮别人做而不是做自己被分配的任务。
  • Jumping on fires even when not on-call.即使不在值班也跑去救火。
  • Working on side projects instead of the main project.做副项目而不是主项目。
— 第 122 页 —
  • Excessive testing (rare).过度测试（少见）。
  • Excessive automation (rare).过度自动化（少见）。

Individual contributors often get stuck when they need to:

独立贡献者在需要做以下事情时经常卡住：

  • Finish the last 10–20% of a project.完成项目最后 10-20%。
  • Start a project completely from scratch.完全从零开始一个项目。
  • Do project planning (You need me to write what now? A roadmap?).做项目计划（你要我写什么？路线图？）。
  • Work with unfamiliar code/libraries/systems.和不熟悉的代码/库/系统打交道。
  • Work with other teams (please don't make me go sit with data engineering!!).和其他团队合作（求别让我去和数据工程坐一起！！）。
  • Talk to other people (in engineering, or more commonly, outside of engineering).和其他人说话（工程内，或者更常见的是工程外）。
  • Ask for help (far beyond the point they realized they were stuck and needed help).求助（远在他们意识到自己卡住需要帮助之后很久）。
  • Deal with surprises or unexpected setbacks.处理意外或意想不到的挫折。
  • Navigate bureaucracy.在官僚体系中穿行。
  • Pull the trigger and going into prod.扣扳机上生产。
  • Deal with vendors/external partners.和供应商/外部伙伴打交道。
  • Say no, because they can't seem to just say no (instead of saying no they just go into avoidance mode, or worse, always say yes).说不，因为他们似乎就是说不出口（不说不，他们就进入回避模式，或者更糟，永远说好）。

"AHA! Wait! Camille is missing something! People don't always get stuck!" This is true. Although almost everyone has some areas in which they find themselves overly hung up, some people also get sloppy instead of getting stuck. Sloppy looks like never getting sidetracked from the main project but never finishing anything completely, letting the finishing touches of the last project drop as you rush heedlessly into the next project.

「啊！等等！Camille 漏了什么！人们不总是卡住！」这是真的。虽然几乎每个人都有一些发现自己过度纠结的领域，但有些人不是卡住而是变草率。草率看起来像从不从主项目跑偏但从不完整完成任何事，在你不顾一切冲进下一个项目时，上一个项目的收尾工作就掉了。

— 第 123 页 —

Noticing how people get stuck is a super power, and one that great tech leads and managers rely on to get big things done. When you know how people get stuck, you can plan your projects to rely on people for their strengths and provide them help or even completely side-step their weaknesses. You know who is good to ask for which kinds of help, and who hates that particular challenge just as much as you do.

注意人们怎么卡住是一个超能力，优秀的技术负责人和经理靠它来完成大事。当你知道人们怎么卡住，你可以规划项目依赖人们的优势，给他们帮助甚至完全绕开他们的弱点。你知道谁适合问什么类型的帮助，谁和你一样讨厌那个特定挑战。

The secret is that all of us end up stuck and sidetracked sometimes. There's actually nothing particularly bad about this. Showing people how it happens allows them to decide how to address the issue. They can try to overcome the fears that are sticking them, such as lack of knowledge, skills, or confidence. They can consciously avoid such tasks as much as possible. And best of all, they are now aware of their habits and can use extra diligence when tackling these areas.

秘密是我们所有人最终都会卡住和跑偏。这其实没有什么特别糟糕的。向人们展示它怎么发生让他们决定怎么解决问题。他们可以尝试克服困住他们的恐惧，比如缺乏知识、技能或信心。他们可以有意识地尽量避免这类任务。最好的是，他们现在意识到了自己的习惯，可以在处理这些领域时格外用心。

So, use these lists to pay attention and bring specifics the next time you need to give feedback. No one likes to feel stuck, and they'll be grateful you are there to help dig them out.

所以，用这些列表来注意，下次你需要给反馈时带上具体例子。没有人喜欢感觉卡住，他们会感激你在那里帮他们挖出来。
